Q5651.reason: An 'as is' clause doesn't bar claims for express descriptions of the goods, and the advertised model year was a description that became part of the bargain, so Carol can recover without proving the seller was careless.

Q5672.reason: If the principal's killing was justified by self-defense, it was not a crime, so the instigator has no derivative accomplice liability, while insanity and diminished capacity are personal excuses that don't shield the defendant.

Q8537.reason: A value-neutral definition of punishment lets competing justifications be debated afterward instead of being settled inside the definition itself.
